projects.name: TRINETRA
projects.summary: Recover once when the provider times out.
projects.evidenceTitle: accepted timeout → one replay-safe recovery path
projects.problem: A provider can accept a payment and time out before confirmation. A blind retry risks a duplicate submission, while the payer and operator still need one explainable history.
projects.constraint: Replay safety, provider recovery and ordered risk evidence must survive across API replicas without turning a pending state into a retry instruction.
projects.decision: Keep payment and provider-attempt history in a tenant-scoped ledger, reuse the original idempotent resource on replay, then resolve uncertainty through status inquiry.
projects.result: The synthetic accepted-timeout checkpoint and PostgreSQL/Redis integration test exercise one provider submission, cross-replica replay and recovery to the original payment.

projects.name: TRISHUL
projects.summary: Trace money while uncertainty stays visible.
projects.evidenceTitle: cash-out forecast → explicit PASS or ABSTAIN
projects.problem: After a fraud complaint, investigators need to trace attributable exposure and assess probable cash-out behaviour without presenting incomplete signals as certainty.
projects.constraint: Money can commingle, records arrive from authorised sources at different times, and location and time may have different levels of support.
projects.decision: Build a provenance-backed case graph, represent exposure as a range, and gate geo and time forecasts independently so either dimension can abstain.
projects.result: The prediction and API tests cover supported forecasts, partial evidence, stationary funds and intentional abstention without inventing candidates.

projects.name: MIRA
projects.summary: Publish only after evidence clears the gate.
projects.evidenceTitle: autonomous publishing → threshold, memory and audit
projects.problem: An autonomous editor can repeat stories, amplify weak sources or publish hype while hiding why a candidate was accepted or rejected.
projects.constraint: The agent must continue after initialization, limit each cycle, survive refreshes and retain evidence for both publication and rejection.
projects.decision: Separate discovery, editorial scoring, durable decision memory and publishing; enforce source gates, a fixed threshold and duplicate fingerprints.
projects.result: The backend and policy tests exercise one-item pacing, rejected candidates, later backlog publication and duplicate suppression in durable memory.

projects.name: SOCRATES
projects.summary: Teach the AI. Expose the misconception.
projects.problem: A learner can sound confident while missing a core misconception, so completion alone cannot show whether the concept was understood.
projects.constraint: Evaluation must remain repeatable and explainable even when no LLM key is available.
projects.decision: Seed known misconceptions and score the learner's correction, reasoning and evidence with a transparent stage-based rubric.
projects.result: The rubric maps each learning stage to observable signals and returns the evidence span used by the scoring flow.

projects.name: COUNSELFLOW
projects.summary: Resolve conflicts before locking a list.
projects.evidenceTitle: preference list → conflict audit before lock
projects.problem: A candidate can receive a plausible college list that violates their branch priority, budget, distance or hard exclusions and still lock it by mistake.
projects.constraint: Official cutoff evidence, hard constraints and soft preferences must remain distinguishable, deterministic and reviewable after every edit.
projects.decision: Generate an ordered strategy, surface coded contradictions, mark the audit stale after edits and block lock while a critical conflict remains.
projects.result: Domain tests exercise eight conflict rules, reproducible strategy hashes and the invariant that unresolved critical conflicts prevent lock.

projects.name: PAPERTRADE
projects.summary: Keep price and portfolio state authoritative.
projects.evidenceTitle: changing market session → one authoritative execution path
projects.problem: A trading simulator must keep orders and portfolio state credible when client prices drift, the exchange closes or the live price provider is unavailable.
projects.constraint: The server owns execution price and holdings while the interface still needs useful market behaviour outside NSE live hours.
projects.decision: Canonicalize symbols, resolve execution prices on the backend, persist transactions and switch between live and bounded simulated market sessions.
projects.result: Backend tests cover NSE live boundaries, weekends, published holidays, the special Sunday session and time-bucketed simulated candles.
projects.stack: React · Express · MongoDB · SSE · Yahoo Finance
